extracted.intended_audience: agency contracting officers, acquisition personnel, and heads of executive departments and establishments
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for deciding whether commercial/industrial type work should be performed by contract or in-house, and the procedures for cost comparisons, justifications, and related contracting practices under OMB Circular A-76 and associated recommendations for DoD/Navy contracting offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish and maintain internal milestones and milestone integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal milestones should be established and milestone integrity maintained. This is best accomplished by active management attention of the Contracting Officer early in the cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide realistic standards (e.g., Procurement Administrative Lead Time goals) to field activities, monitor attainment of standards, and recognize unique CITA characteristics that may preclude attainment of existing PAL time goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitize procurement agreements between commands
rubrics_metrics.description: Naval Supply Systems Command and the Naval Facilities Engineering Command definitize the agreements as to which command will procure a specific service function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifying which command procures a function assists development of specialized expertise at contracting offices and enhances coordination, preparation, and submission of statements of work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish dedicated training programs for contracting offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting offices establish dedicated training programs centered around the key reference material noted in this research effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training should be focused on the relevant reference materials identified by the research to build subject-matter competence in CITA support service contracting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support internal planning efforts to assure realistic milestones and accurate SOWs
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting offices attempt to be more supportive of the internal planning efforts of the Task Group to assure establishment of realistic milestones, preparation and submission of accurate and complete statements of work, and maintenance of the integrity of the system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate and develop schedules with supported organizations early in the planning cycle and before receipt of the purchase request in the contracting office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revise and clarify directives to conform with policy guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Department of Defense and Navy directives be revised and clarified to conform with existing policy guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarified directives will enhance the ability of field contracting offices to achieve consistent policy implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide separate regulatory coverage for service contracting (CITA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate coverage of service contracting be included in the Defense Acquisition Regulation including a distinct section on CITA Support Service Contracting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This should address clause usage inconsistencies, procedures for 8(a) set-asides, use of options and cost comparison process, methodologies for determining low private sector bid/offer, treatment of late submission of the Government in-house estimate, and determination of significant discrepancy in the Government estimate; consider incorporating Firm Bid/Offer procedure (DAR Case 76-144).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assure the integrity of contracting professionals and processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting professionals should take aggressive action to assure the integrity of the system is above reproach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting Officers should assess their own actions for inadvertent compromising positions; procurement personnel familiar with Standards of Conduct should provide assistance and guidance to Task Group members to ensure understanding of duties and responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use formal advertising for Cost Comparison in conversions
rubrics_metrics.description: In most instances, formal advertising methods should be used to accomplish the Cost Comparison for potential conversions of in-house to contractor performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require submission of a performance-oriented statement of work detailing what is to be accomplished but not how it is to be done.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make maximum use of pre-bid/pre-proposal conferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting offices should make maximum use of pre-bid/pre-proposal conferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These conferences help contractors understand new concepts/procedures in CITA contracting and require contract negotiators to be familiar with the cost comparison process to answer questions intelligently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat Government as another potential source to preserve equitability
rubrics_metrics.description: To preserve equitability and integrity, Contracting Officers should consider the Government as simply another potential source of supply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures for submission of in-house cost estimates, negotiations, distribution of solicitation amendments, etc., should be the same for the Government as for other potential contractors; consider Task Group Chairperson equivalent to private sector manager and direct communications accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider additional Government costs as award factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting Officers emphasize that the additional Government costs to be incurred if a contract is released are award factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make clear the distinction between contractors' quoted price and the total cost to the Government should a contract be awarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure contracting personnel involved in bid/public openings review directives
rubrics_metrics.description: Contract negotiators and personnel who will be directly involved in a Bid or Public Opening for contracting-out actions review existing CITA directives to ensure the process will be accomplished in a professional manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review directives to ensure compliance and professionalism during bidding/opening procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracting Officers understand appeals concept in Circular
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting Officers review the guidance in the Circular to assure they have a firm understanding of the appeals concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understanding appeals is significant for placing the Contracting Officer's role in both appeal and protest processes in proper perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose — determine contract vs in-house performance
rubrics_metrics.description: This Circular establishes the policies and procedures used to determine whether needed commercial or industrial type work should be done by contract with private sources or in-house using Government facilities and personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Circular (and supplementing guidance) as the administrative direction for making contracting vs in-house decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy precept: Rely on the private sector
rubrics_metrics.description: Where private sources are available, they should be looked to first to provide the commercial or industrial goods and services needed by the Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Government's business is not to be in business; rely on competitive private enterprise when feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy precept: Retain inherently governmental functions in-house
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain functions are inherently governmental in nature and must be performed by Government personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functions intimately related to public interest (e.g., discretional application of government authority) should remain in-house.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy precept: Aim for economy using cost comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: When private performance is feasible and no overriding factors require in-house performance, rigorous comparison of contract costs versus in-house costs should be used to decide how the work will be done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost comparisons should be rigorous and aimed at delivering the most economical performance for taxpayers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Government commercial or industrial activity
rubrics_metrics.description: An activity operated and managed by a Federal executive agency which provides a product or service that could be obtained from a private source; must be separable and regularly needed, operational in nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activity must be suitable for performance either in-house or by contract and not a one-time short-duration activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Expansion thresholds and new start
rubrics_metrics.description: An 'expansion' involves additional capital investment of $100,000 or more, or increasing annual operating costs by $200,000 or more, provided the increase exceeds 20%; an expansion increasing capital or operating cost by 100% or more is a 'new start.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consolidations only count if proposed totals exceed thresholds; these numeric thresholds determine applicability of Circular provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'conversion' is the transfer of work from a Government commercial or industrial activity to performance by a private commercial source under contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversions trigger cost comparison and other Circular procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Private commercial source
rubrics_metrics.description: A private business, university, or other non-Federal activity located in the United States (and territories) which provides a commercial or industrial product or service required by Government agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Source location limited to U.S., territories, District of Columbia, and Puerto Rico for purposes of the Circular.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Governmental functions categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Governmental functions include (1) discretionary application of Government authority (e.g., investigations, prosecutions, management of national defense), (2) monetary transactions and entitlements (e.g., benefit programs, tax collection), and (3) in-house core R&D capabilities needed for technical analysis, evaluation, and technology base management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core R&D capability may be retained in-house; services beyond justified core capability are not governmental functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: agencies must follow Circular provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: No executive agency will engage in or contract for commercial or industrial activities except in accordance with the provisions of this Circular, or as otherwise provided by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation provisions do not apply to governmental functions; applies to GOCO new starts/expansions; additional constraints (e.g., cannot be used as contract authority).

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional restrictions on Circular use
rubrics_metrics.description: The Circular does not provide authority to enter into contracts; will not be used to create employer-employee relationships, to justify conversion solely to meet personnel ceilings, nor to contradict other laws or applicable acquisition regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow acquisition regulations for contract authority; consult Federal Personnel Manual on employee-like contract relationships; major system acquisitions governed by A-109; consulting services of purely advisory nature excluded; printing/binding applicability limited by law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use preference for products/services from other Federal agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Excess property and services available from other Federal agencies should be used in preference to new starts or contracts unless private sector is more economical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where excess capacity exists, it can be used to provide services to other agencies; if formal management program exists (e.g., ADP sharing), reported excess can be used without further justification; otherwise cost justification required and competitive solicitations should establish commercial costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on creating/expanding capacity to serve other agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should not create or expand capacity for the purpose of providing commercially available products or services to other agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If performing agency's own requirements increase making capacity no longer excess, support to other agencies should be terminated with sufficient notice unless exceptional circumstances exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review requirement for activities providing services to other agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Activities operated primarily to provide products or services to other agencies must be reviewed under this Circular to determine whether continued Government operation is justified; review no later than October 1, 1981.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior to review, agencies may use such services without further justification; approval of continued operation allows use up to approved capability without further justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition authorizing government operation: No satisfactory commercial source
rubrics_metrics.description: A Government activity can be authorized without a comparative cost analysis when there is no private commercial source capable of providing the needed product or service or use of private source would cause unacceptable delay or disruption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency must make all reasonable efforts to identify sources, including placing at least three notices in the Commerce Business Daily over 90 days (two notices over 30 days for urgent requirements), and obtain assistance from GSA, SBA, and Commerce; conclusions about unacceptable delay/disruption require specific documented explanation with cost, time, and performance measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insufficient justifications for in-house performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors such as involvement in classified program, being part of an agency's basic mission, or possibility of strike by contract employees are not adequate justification for in-house performance on their own; urgency alone is not sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must show commercial sources are not able and Government can provide service when needed; transitory disruption from conversions not sufficient; specify why circumstances differ if activity has been contracted elsewhere or previously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition authorizing government operation: National defense exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: A Government activity operated by military personnel may be justified when (a) personnel are utilized in/subject to deployment in direct combat support, (b) activity essential for training in exclusively military skills, or (c) activity needed to provide appropriate work assignments for career progression or rotation base for overseas assignments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depot/intermediate level maintenance may be justified per Secretary of Defense-approved criteria limiting extent of in-house capability; such justifications require detailed explanation and high-level approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition authorizing government operation: Higher cost justification
rubrics_metrics.description: A Government activity may be authorized if a comparative cost analysis indicates the Government can provide the product or service at a lower total cost than if obtained from a private commercial source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparative cost analysis must be prepared in accordance with the Circular and Cost Comparison Handbook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost Comparisons requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision for in-house performance based on economy must be supported by a comparative cost analysis prepared in accordance with this Circular and the Cost Comparison Handbook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Handbook's instructions for determining the total cost to Government for each alternative to achieve accurate cost-based decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common ground rule: same scope and level of performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Both Government and commercial cost figures must be based on the same scope of work and the same level of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare a sufficiently precise work statement with performance standards that can be monitored for either mode of performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common ground rule: use of standard cost factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard cost factors will be used as prescribed by the Cost Comparison Handbook and supplemented by agencies for particular operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must defend any variations in costing from one case to another.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common ground rule: aim at full cost
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost comparisons are to be aimed at full cost, to the maximum extent practical in all cases; all significant Government costs (including allocation of overhead and indirect costs) must be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include costs for direct Government performance and for administration of a contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation guidance for continuing workloads
rubrics_metrics.description: In solicitations for workloads of a continuing nature, solicitations should, unless inappropriate, provide for prepriced options or renewal options for the out-years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepriced/renewal options guard against 'buy-in' pricing, provide continuity of operation, potential lower contract prices when contractor provides equipment/facilities, and reduced disruption. Recompetition also guards against buy-ins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Threshold for conducting cost comparison studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordinarily, agencies should not incur the delay and expense of conducting cost comparison studies to justify a Government activity for products or services estimated to be less than $100,000 in annual operating costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities below this threshold should be performed by contract unless justified under other Circular provisions (e.g., no satisfactory commercial source or national defense); if inadequate competition or other factors cause unreasonable commercial prices, a cost comparison study may be conducted after reasonable efforts to obtain satisfactory prices.
